children.title: DOJ and FBI Say Their Epstein Review Found No Incriminating Client List
children.description_short: DOJ and FBI Say Their Epstein Review Found No Incriminating Client List
children.description_medium: On July 7, 2025, the Justice Department and FBI released a memorandum describing a review of investigative holdings relating to Jeffrey Epstein. The agencies said the review found no incriminating “client list,” no credible evidence Epstein blackmailed prominent individuals, and no evidence to predicate an investigation of uncharged third parties. The memorandum says victim privacy and court seals limited disclosure.
children.description_long: The Justice Department and FBI’s July 7, 2025 memorandum described a review of investigative holdings relating to Jeffrey Epstein and the agencies’ decision about further disclosure. It said FBI personnel searched digital systems and physical storage locations, then had agents, analysts, attorneys, and privacy and civil-liberties experts review the material. The agencies said the files included images and videos involving minors and identifying information about victims; it also said much of the material was subject to court-ordered sealing. The memorandum stated that the review found no incriminating “client list,” no credible evidence Epstein blackmailed prominent individuals, and no evidence that could predicate an investigation of uncharged third parties. It described Epstein as having harmed more than one thousand victims and said no further disclosure was appropriate or warranted. These are the government’s stated conclusions about its review; the memorandum does not say every person associated with Epstein was investigated or exonerated. This record covers the July review and its public findings alone. It does not treat the memo as proof of the separate birthday-message dispute or the later DOJ investigation request.

children.title: Trump Sues Wall Street Journal over Epstein Birthday-Note Report
children.description_short: Trump sued the Wall Street Journal over its report about a 2003 Epstein birthday greeting.
children.description_medium: Reuters reported that Trump filed a defamation suit on July 18, 2025, seeking at least $10 billion from the Wall Street Journal and related defendants over its report about a 2003 birthday greeting to Jeffrey Epstein. Trump denied the report, and Reuters said it had not verified the underlying account. The suit’s allegations were not a court finding.
children.description_long: Reuters reported that President Donald Trump filed a defamation suit on July 18, 2025, against the Wall Street Journal and its owners, including Rupert Murdoch, seeking at least $10 billion. The lawsuit followed the newspaper’s report that Trump’s name appeared on a 2003 birthday greeting for Jeffrey Epstein with a sexually suggestive drawing and a reference to secrets they shared. Reuters said the complaint alleged that the story defamed Trump and caused financial and reputational harm. Trump denied the Journal’s account, and Reuters stated that it had not independently verified the underlying report. This record treats the filing as a confirmed legal action and the birthday message as an allegation in reporting that Trump disputed. A complaint’s allegations do not establish defamation, and a reported denial does not resolve whether the message existed or who wrote it. The suit is a separate July event from the Justice Department and FBI’s review memorandum and from the later announcement that federal prosecutors would examine Epstein’s ties to political figures. This description does not imply any court ruling or final result in the case.

children.title: Trump Requests Epstein-Ties Inquiry; DOJ Assigns Jay Clayton
children.description_short: Trump requested a DOJ inquiry into Epstein’s ties to Clinton and others; Bondi assigned Jay Clayton.
children.description_medium: Reuters reported on November 14, 2025, that the Justice Department would fulfill Trump’s request to investigate Jeffrey Epstein’s ties to Bill Clinton and JPMorgan. Attorney General Pam Bondi said Manhattan U.S. Attorney Jay Clayton would lead the inquiry; Trump also named Larry Summers and Reid Hoffman. The report describes an announced investigation, not charges or findings against the people named.
children.description_long: On November 14, 2025, Reuters reported that the Justice Department would fulfill President Donald Trump’s request to investigate Jeffrey Epstein’s ties to former President Bill Clinton and JPMorgan. Attorney General Pam Bondi said Jay Clayton, the top federal prosecutor in Manhattan, would lead the investigation. Reuters reported that Trump also asked the department to examine former Treasury Secretary Larry Summers and Reid Hoffman, and that all three men had been mentioned in documents released by the House Oversight Committee. The article said the department’s decision came despite a July memorandum in which DOJ and the FBI said they had found no evidence that could predicate an investigation against uncharged third parties. Reuters characterized Trump as seeking to shift attention from his own relationship with Epstein and noted that the inquiry could face a challenge as vindictive prosecution; these are attributed reporting and analysis, not judicial findings. This record covers the request and announced assignment only. It does not say that charges were filed, that investigators reached conclusions, or that the named individuals committed wrongdoing.
